Thermal management: chillers · cooling towers · chilled water · MAU · DCC · waste-heat recovery

Chilled water for MAU cooling coils about 5–7 °C (paper); in dual-temperature chilled water systems, low temperature about 6–7 °C (MAU) and high temperature about 15–18 °C (DCC) (company technical article)
MAU sequence in the literature: fan → preheat coil → precool coil → humidifier (air washer) → cooling coil → reheat coil
The DCC runs with the coil surface above the return-air dew point so that no condensation forms (hence 'dry')

Chilled water headers are placed in the return-shaft bands and the central core and do not cross above the FFU ceiling (whether this reduces the risk of water leaks falling into the cleanroom is a review hypothesis).
PCW: process cooling water closed loop
PCW heat exchanger (secondary side) → circulation pump → supply header → bay branches → tools, dry pumps, scrubbers, RF power → return header → heat exchanger
The primary side of the heat exchanger is chilled water (CHW) or cooling tower water. PCW is a closed loop dedicated to tools; it is not consumed or discharged in normal operation
Required temperature in the literature about 13–20 °C (paper)
Measured benchmark case (a fab in Taiwan): supply 17.8 °C, return 21 °C, flow 1,121.9 ㎥/h, cooling capacity 1,187 RT
Check: Q = ρ·V·cp·ΔT = 1000 × (1121.9/3600) × 4.186 × 3.2 ≈ 4,175 kW ≈ 1,187 RT (3.517 kW/RT) → matches the literature figure
PCW temperature, flow and redundancy for Pyeongtaek P1–P4 could not be confirmed from public sources.
Heat exchanger locations (1F and 5F FSF support zones) and header and branch positions are all concept. This is not the result of a hydraulic analysis with pipe sizing or flow calculation.
Gas: bulk gas · specialty gas · filling (transfer) and exchange points
Bulk gas: nearby gas-company plant (air separation unit) → underground pipeline → campus entry → (backup liquid storage and vaporization) → purification → fab CSF header → tools
Specialty gas: delivery of cylinders and bulk containers → gas cabinet or BSGS → distribution (VMB) → tool gas box. Purge and cabinet exhaust are separate systems
Distinction of tasks: bulk storage has a 'transfer/filling connection'; cylinders have an 'exchange work area' (cylinders are not filled on site)
Figures such as pressure, purity and storage quantity vary by supplier and process and are not included in this model (unsupported figures excluded).

Hazardous emissions (air): exhaust segregation and treatment
Process tool → (where needed) dry pump and POU treatment → dedicated exhaust header matching the stream → central treatment equipment → fan → stack (treated exhaust)
Segregation: acid / alkali (ammonia) / organic (VOC, solvent) / heat and general. Mixing causes reactions and solids, so they are collected separately
POU → rooftop scrubber → stack is one of several arrangements; the type and presence of POU depend on the process
Exhaust classification in the literature: heat/general / acid / (optional) ammonia / VOC. Heat exhaust is often released without treatment (patent literature)
VOC: zeolite concentrator rotor + thermal oxidizer; acid and alkali: central wet scrubber (paper)
Acid gases are treated in wet scrubbers by contact with a neutralizing solution (vendor technical material)
